card.name: Punctuation after lipid-related terms
card.fires_on: Punctuation (an opening parenthesis or comma) or a linking word right after a fat- or lipid-related term such as triglyceride transfer protein, castor oil, or lipid emulsions. It also fires on commas in inactive-ingredient lists.

modes.label: Bracket after lipid term
modes.description: An opening parenthesis follows a lipid-related phrase, often introducing an abbreviation or example.
modes.example: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein<< (>>MTTP) Inhibitor: l

modes.label: Comma in ingredient lists
modes.description: A comma follows an ingredient name, such as an oil or dye, in a list of inactive ingredients.
modes.example: (testosterone undecanoate<<,>> refined castor oil, benzyl ben

card.writes: It seems to suppress lipid and lip-related word continuations, so a lipid word is not repeated right after the punctuation.
card.plain: It fires on the comma or bracket that comes right after a fat or oil term in a drug label.
